data.long_meaning: Arin is derived from the Sanskrit word 'aruna' which means red or dawn. In Hindu mythology, Arin is associated with the god Aruna, the charioteer of the sun god Surya. The name is also believed to represent strength and courage. The name Arin carries the meaning “Mountain, strong one” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Arin usually hope their child will grow to embody mountain, strong one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Arin was a famous sage mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Sanskrit epic. The name Arin carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Arin is known for his wisdom and is a disciple of the sage Vyasa. He is also one of the eight great sages (Atharvana Rishis) who were invited to the great assembly of gods and demons to churn the ocean of milk to obtain the elixir of immortality.

historical_references.reference: Arin is also the name of a king in ancient Indian history who ruled over the Kingdom of Magadha around 500 BCE.
historical_references.context: Arin is mentioned in Buddhist texts as a patron of the Buddha Siddhartha Gautama. He is known to have provided the Buddha with food and shelter during his wanderings.
